claims.text: Builder pattern: a builder object collects an object's settings over several steps, then one final call creates the finished object; collecting and creating are kept apart.
claims.source_hint: glossary builder-pattern; GoF book, Builder pattern (principle only, no director)

claims.text: WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args) returns a WebApplicationBuilder; registrations are added to builder.Services (an IServiceCollection); builder.Build() returns the WebApplication, whose Services property resolves the registered services and whose Run() starts the server.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: WebApplication and WebApplicationBuilder (fundamentals/minimal-apis/webapplication); API ref WebApplicationBuilder.Build

claims.text: After builder.Build(), builder.Services is read-only: adding a registration (even a duplicate like AddScoped<OrderService>()) throws System.InvalidOperationException "The service collection cannot be modified because it is read-only." at run time, before app.Run().
claims.source_hint: Run at stage-1 (verified locally, .NET SDK 10): exception from ServiceCollection.ThrowReadOnlyException; API ref ServiceCollection.MakeReadOnly / IsReadOnly

claims.text: The C# compiler does not reject a builder.Services.Add... call placed after Build(): the project builds, and the error appears only when the code runs.
claims.source_hint: Run at stage-1 (dotnet run builds, then throws at startup)

claims.text: At stage-1 Program.cs: CreateBuilder on line 10; builder.Services lines from 13 to AddCors (49-50) each add registrations (AddControllers, AddDonHangInfrastructure add several); Build() on line 52; the migration block after it only resolves DonHangDbContext from app.Services.

claims.text: AddDonHangInfrastructure (in DonHang.Infrastructure) adds registrations to the same IServiceCollection that Program.cs adds to afterwards.

DbContextOptionsBuilder<TContext>: UseNpgsql(connectionString) configures the context to use PostgreSQL through the Npgsql EF Core provider; the Options property returns the built DbContextOptions<TContext>, which is passed to the DbContext constructor.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: DbContext configuration (DbContextOptionsBuilder, 'Options' passed to constructor); Npgsql EF Core provider docs: UseNpgsql

claims.text: DesignTimeDbContextFactory.CreateDbContext creates a DbContextOptionsBuilder<DonHangDbContext>, calls UseNpgsql with a design-time-only connection string, and returns new DonHangDbContext(builder.Options); it is used by dotnet ef at design time.

A C# object initializer (new Order { CustomerId = ..., Status = ... }) creates the object and sets the listed properties within one expression; OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync sets CustomerId, PlacedAt, Status and Items this way at stage-1.
claims.source_hint: C# docs: Object and collection initializers; examples/don-hang @ stage-1: DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs:12-18

claims.text: A builder pays off when settings arrive in separate steps, possibly from different code, before the object can be created. When every value is known at once and no step must finish first, an object initializer is enough.
